glossary.definition: An embedded sign-in: the authorize request is answered with JSON describing a flow and its status, not with a redirect to a hosted login page. The client (usually a BFF) then drives the flow one step at a time. This lab signs in this way only. Modelled on the public PingOne sample apps; details are UNVERIFIED against a real tenant.

The classic authorization-code login: the browser is redirected to a hosted sign-in page and back. This lab refuses it on purpose (scenario S08): an authorize request without response_mode=pi.flow gets an error and no flow or cookie. Contrast with pi.flow, where the user never leaves the application.

Where a pi.flow flow is: USERNAME_PASSWORD_REQUIRED, then DEVICE_SELECTION_REQUIRED and OTP_REQUIRED when MFA applies, then RESUME_REQUIRED, then COMPLETED. These names are the mock's. A real PingOne has more statuses (policy screens, external IdP steps) and the exact names are UNVERIFIED here.

A cookie that binds a flow to one client. In this mock it is replaced on every step, and a flow call or resume with an old or missing cookie is 401 INVALID_SESSION_TOKEN. The cookie name and the exact rotation points are UNVERIFIED against a real PingOne. The page never sees the real value (HttpOnly); it shows the server's shortened preview.

RFC 7636. The client sends a hash of a secret verifier with the authorize request and the verifier with the token request, so a stolen code is useless. This lab requires S256, state and nonce, and burns a code on its first use.

acr says how strongly the user authenticated; amr lists the methods used (pwd, otp, mfa, ciba). The acr strings in this lab, mock:single and mock:multi, are invented. Which acr strings a real PingOne issues is UNVERIFIED.

auth_time is when the user last authenticated. A resource server can demand a recent one (max_age). In this mock every authorize is a fresh login, so max_age is satisfied by the new login; real SSO-session behaviour is not modelled.

A resource server refuses a token that proves too little with 401 and WWW-Authenticate: Bearer error="insufficient_user_authentication", acr_values and/or max_age. The client re-authorizes with those values and retries. The RFC is the standard; whether PingOne supports it this way is UNVERIFIED.

The client asks the server to authenticate a user on their own device (POST /bc-authorize), then polls the token endpoint. States seen while polling: authorization_pending, slow_down (poll slower), access_denied (the user said no), expired_token (too late). In the lab a MOCK PHONE approves or denies.

A short text shown on both the client and the user's device so the user can tell which request they are approving. This mock limits it to 8 characters; that limit is the mock's own value and the real limit is UNVERIFIED.

A request header, 00-<32 hex trace id>-<16 hex span id>-01, that ties the hops of one run together. Every request this lab makes carries one (one trace id per run, a new span id per hop) and the mock answers with the same trace id and a new span id, so a trace can be followed across the page, the BFF and the mock.
A stand-in in the UI for the user's device in CIBA: it shows the notification and has Approve and Deny buttons that call the mock's /phone endpoints. It is not a PingOne feature.

stories.title: Happy path: Mark Ellison signs in to Mock Air with pi.flow
stories.say: Four calls and no browser redirect: open the flow, post the password, resume, exchange the code. The tokens carry acr, amr, auth_time, sub and the nonce.

stories.title: Mark Ellison mistypes the password once, then succeeds
stories.say: A wrong password does not kill the flow. It stays at USERNAME_PASSWORD_REQUIRED with an error and an attempt counter.

stories.title: Mark Ellison's Mock Air sign-in locks after three wrong passwords
stories.say: After the limit even the right password is refused until the lock lapses.

stories.title: Resume with a stale session-token cookie is rejected
stories.say: The cookie changes on every step. Replaying an older one at /resume is refused; the current one still works.

stories.title: A flow left open too long expires
stories.say: Flows live five minutes in this mock. After that the credentials step is refused and the client must start over.

stories.title: An authorization code is used twice
stories.say: The code is single use. The second exchange is invalid_grant.

stories.title: The token request carries the wrong PKCE verifier
stories.say: The code is bound to the S256 challenge from step 1. A different verifier is refused and the code is burned.

stories.title: A redirect-based login attempt is refused
stories.say: This lab signs in with pi.flow only. Without response_mode=pi.flow the authorize request is an error and no flow or cookie is issued.

stories.title: Mark Ellison signs in with a password, then the booking change asks for more
stories.say: The resource answers 401 with an RFC 9470 challenge naming a mock acr. The client re-authorizes with acr_values, the engine forces MFA, and the retry succeeds. The acr names are mock.

stories.title: Dana Okafor's authentication is too old for the booking change
stories.say: The token is fine and strong enough, but auth_time is older than the resource allows. The challenge carries max_age; a fresh sign-in fixes it.

stories.title: CIBA: Mark Ellison approves on the mock phone
stories.say: The client starts a backchannel request, polls (authorization_pending), the mock phone approves, the next poll returns tokens.

stories.title: CIBA: Mark Ellison denies on the mock phone
stories.say: A denial ends the request: the next poll is access_denied.

stories.title: CIBA: nobody answers in time
stories.say: Past expires_in the poll returns expired_token.

stories.title: CIBA: the client polls too fast
stories.say: Polling inside the interval returns slow_down and the interval grows by five seconds.

stories.title: CIBA: the binding message is too long
stories.say: The mock limits binding_message to 8 characters and refuses a longer one with invalid_binding_message. The limit is a mock value, not verified against a real tenant.

stories.title: Priya Nair signs in with a password and a one-time passcode
stories.say: Two enrolled devices means DEVICE_SELECTION_REQUIRED, then OTP_REQUIRED, then RESUME_REQUIRED. The token's acr is mock:multi and amr lists the factors.
